filename: A U.S. scientific community review of carbon cycle science gaps and opportunities to better support earth system science and carbon management.pdf
title: A U.S. scientific community review of carbon cycle science gaps and opportunities to better support earth system science and carbon management
testbed_rationale: This paper is a review article and perspective outlining observational and modeling strategies for operational greenhouse gas and carbon cycle monitoring; it does not produce or distribute a machine learning parameterization benchmark dataset.
pain_points: Observational data droughts in tropical, Arctic, and Southern Ocean regions due to cloud cover, seasonal darkness, and sparse in-situ infrastructure
Discrepancies between top-down atmospheric inverse flux estimates and bottom-up national greenhouse gas inventories or terrestrial biosphere models
High computational cost limiting uncertainty quantification in high-resolution atmospheric transport inversions
Signal saturation of radar backscatter in high-biomass forests and spatial sampling gaps of spaceborne lidar altimetry
Sub-national fossil fuel CO2 emissions are highly uncertain due to disaggregation assumptions and risk aliasing into natural flux estimates
Lack of long-term operational continuity guarantees for research-focused satellite missions observing greenhouse gases and biomass
extraction_notes: A corrigendum attached to the article (Earth-Science Reviews 280 (2026) 105553) noted the administrative removal of co-authors S.C. Reed and L. Windham-Myers due to USGS agency internal approval processes, and added a disclaimer for NOAA co-author L. Bruhwiler. Both authors are listed in the original article and retained here with this note.
